questions.q: The charge flowing in a conductor changes with time as $Q\left(t\right) = \alphat - \betat^{2} + \gammat^{3}$,~where $\alpha, \beta$~and $\gamma$& are constants. Minimum value of current is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& $Q = \left(\alphat - \betat^{2} + \gammat^{3}\right)

Current flowing through conductor is given by~

$i = $\dfrac{d Q}{d t} = \left(\alpha -$2\betat + 3\gammat^{2}\right) . . . \left($1\right)$

For current to be minimum,~$\dfrac{d i}{d t} =0$

So,~$\dfrac{d i}{d t} = \left(6\gammat - $2\beta\right) =$0$

$⇒ t = \dfrac{β}{3\gamma}$

Substituting in equation (1),

$i = \left(\alpha -$2\betat + 3\gammat^{2}\right) = $\alpha --2\beta \left(\dfrac{β}{3\gamma}\right) ++$3\gamma\left(\dfrac{β}{3\gamma})$2 = \alpha $--2\dfrac{\beta2}{3\gamma} +$++3\dfrac{\beta2}{9\gamma} = \left(\alpha - \dfrac{\beta2}{3\gamma}\right)$

questions.q: A conducting wire of length $l$, area of crosssection $A$~and electric resistivity $ρ$ is connected between the terminals of a battery. A potential difference $V$ is developed between its ends, causing an electric current. If the length of the wire of the same material is doubled and the area of cross-section is halved, the resultant current would be___
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As per the question&

Resistance $= ρ\left(2l\right)\left(A / 2\right) = \dfrac{4ρl}{A}$

$⇒$ Current $= \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{VA}{4ρl}$

questions.solution:
Let voltmeter reading is& $v$

$\dfrac{v}{100} \times 400 + \left(\dfrac{v}{10000} + \dfrac{v}{400}\right)800 = 6$

$⇒ v + \dfrac{8v}{100} + 2v = 6; \dfrac{77v}{25} = 6; v = \dfrac{150}{77} = 1 . 95v$

questions.q: Two identical cells each of emf $1 . 5V$ are connected in parallel across a parallel combination of two resistors each of resistance $20Ω$. A voltmeter connected in the circuit measures $1 . 2V$. The internal resistance of each cell is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Equivalent resistance of the parallel& $20Ω$~branches will be~$10Ω$.

Equivalent EMF of the two branches which are in parallel will be,~$= \dfrac{\dfrac{1 . 5}{r} + \dfrac{1 . 5}{r}}{\dfrac{1}{r} + \dfrac{1}{r}} = 1 . 5V$~and the equivalent internal resistance for same branches will be,~$\dfrac{r}{2}$.

For loop containing voltmeter and~$10Ω$~resistor,~$1 . 2 - 10i = 0 ⇒ i = 0 . 12A$.

Reading of voltmeter should be,

$1 . 2 = 1 . 5 - i\left(\dfrac{r}{2}\right) ⇒ i\left(\dfrac{r}{2}\right) = 0 . 3 ⇒ r = \dfrac{0 . 6}{i} = \dfrac{0 . 6}{0 . 12} = 5Ω$

questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & P_{\text {input }}=V i=100 \mathrm{~W} \\ & \eta=\frac{P_{\text {out }}}{P_{\text {input }}}=0.916\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The Wheatstone bridge shown in the figure below, gets balanced when the carbon resistor& used as ${R}_{1}$ has the colour code (orange, red, brown). The resistors ${R}_{2}$ and ${R}_{4}$ are $80Ω$ and $40Ω$, respectively. Assuming that the colour code for the carbon resistors gives their accurate values, the colour code for the carbon resistor, used as ${R}_{3}$, would be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Colour band& $A$~and~$B$~indicate the first two significant figures of resistance in 'ohm', while the~$C$~band gives the decimal multiplier i.e., the number of zeros that follows the two significant figures~$A$~and~$B$.

The last band~$D$~indicates the tolerance in percentage about the indicated value or in other word,~it represents the percentage accuracy of the indicated value.~

For ${R}_{1}$,~the given colour of the rings of a carbon resistor are orange, red, brown then, the value of resistance is

${R}_{1} = 32 \times {10}^{1}$

Condition for balance in the Wheat stone's~bridge is

$\dfrac{R1}{R3} = \dfrac{R2}{R4}$

So, $\dfrac{320}{{R}_{3}} = \dfrac{80}{40}$

$∴ {R}_{3} = 160Ω$, so colour coding of resistor~${R}_{3}$~is

Brown$\to 1$

Blue$\to 6$

Brown$\to 1$
$16 \times {10}^{1} ⇒ 160Ω$

questions.q:
A. The drift velocity of electrons decreases with the increase in the temperature of conductor.
B. The drift velocity is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section of given conductor.
C. The drift velocity does not depend on the applied potential difference to the conductor.
D. The drift velocity of electron is inversely proportional to the length of the conductor.
E. The drift velocity increases with the increase in the temperature of conductor.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Drift velocity $= \left(\dfrac{eτ}{m}\right)E$

${v}_{d} = \left(\dfrac{eτ}{m})\left(\dfrac{\Delta V}{l}\right)

$\Delta V =$ Potential difference applied across the wire As temperature increases, relaxation time decreases, hence ${V}_{d}$ decreases.
As per formula, ${V}_{d} ∝ $\dfrac{1}{l}

${v}_{d} = $\dfrac{I}{neA},as it is not mentioned that current is at steady state neither it is mentioned that $n$ is constant for given conductor. So it can't be said that ${v}_{d}$ is inversely proportional to $A$.

$I = neA{v}_{d} = $\dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{V}{ρl}$A$

${v}_{d} = $\dfrac{eEτ}{m}

$τ$ decrease with temperature increase.

First and fourth statements are correct.

${v}_{d} = $\dfrac{V}{ρlne} \left(E = $\dfrac{V}{l}\right)

questions.q: In the given circuit the internal resistance of the $18V$ cell is negligible. If ${R}_{1} = 400Ω, {R}_{3} = 100Ω$ and ${R}_{4} = 500Ω$ and the reading of an ideal voltmeter across ${R}_{4}$ is $5V,$ then the value of ${R}_{2}$ will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given reading of an ideal voltmeter for resistance& ${R}_{4}$~ is~${V}_{4} = 5V$, then current (let ${i}_{1}$)is~given branch~(as resistance~${R}_{3}$~in series with resistance~${R}_{4}$) is~
${i}_{1} = \dfrac{V}{R4} = \dfrac{5}{500} = 0 . 01A$
Then for resistance~${R}_{3}$, the potential difference will be~

${V}_{3} = {i}_{1}{R}_{3} = 0 . 01 \times 100 = 1V$

So, for given branch of resistance potential difference is

${V}_{3} + {V}_{4} = 1 + 5 = 6V$

From figure for resistance~${R}_{1}, {R}_{3}$~and~${R}_{4}$ a total applied potential difference is~$18V$~then,

${V}_{1} + {V}_{3} + {V}_{4} = 18 ∴ {V}_{1} = 18 - \left({V}_{3} + {V}_{4}\right) = 18 - 6 = 12V$

So, the total current drawn from the source is~

$∴$ Current through ${R}_{2}$

${i}_{2} = 0 \cdot 03 - 0 \cdot 01 = 0 \cdot 02A$
and potential difference for~${R}_{2}$~is~

${V}_{2} = {V}_{3} + {V}_{4} = 6V$~(~${R}_{2}$~is in parallel arrangement with the resistances~${R}_{3}$~and~${R}_{4}$)

Now the value of resistance~${R}_{2}$~is :
~${V}_{2} = {i}_{2}{R}_{2} ⇒ {R}_{2} = \dfrac{V2}{i2} = \dfrac{6}{0 \cdot 02} = 300Ω$

$E = \left(3\right)2 \times R \times 20$

questions.q: A wire of resistance $R$ and length $L$ is cut into $5$ equal parts. If these parts are joined parallely, then resultant resistance will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$Resistance of each part will be equally divided. So, the resistance of each part of the wire can be expressed as $\dfrac{R}{5}$.

The formula to calculate the equivalent resistance of the combination of resistors is given by

$\dfrac{1}{Req} = \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{5}\dfrac{1}{Ri} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

\dfrac{1}{Req} = \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} + \dfrac{5}{R} = \dfrac{25}{R}$⇒ {R}_{eq} = \dfrac{R}{25}$

$

questions.q: A wire of resistance $R$ and radius $r$ is stretched till its radius became $r / 2$. If new resistance of the stretched wire is $x R$, then value of $x$ is _______
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know $\mathrm{R}=\frac{\rho l}{\mathrm{~A}}, \mathrm{R} \propto \frac{l}{\mathrm{r}^2}$
As we starch the wire, its length will increase but its radius will decrease keeping the volume constant
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{i}}=\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{f}} \\
& \pi \mathrm{r}^2 l=\pi \frac{\mathrm{r}^2}{4} l_{\mathrm{f}} \\
& l_{\mathrm{f}}=4 l \\
& \frac{\mathrm{R}_{\text {new }}}{\mathrm{R}_{\text {old }}}=\left(\frac{4 l}{\frac{\mathrm{r}^2}{4}}\right) \frac{\mathrm{r}^2}{l}=16 \\
& \mathrm{R}_{\text {new }}=16 \mathrm{R} \\
\therefore & \mathrm{x}=16
\end{aligned}$
